import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Greedy embedding: Planar graphs*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greedy_embedding%23Planar_graphs)
- [Nöllenburg and Prutkin, *Euclidean Greedy Drawings of Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.5224)
- [Nöllenburg, Prutkin, and Rutter, *On self-approaching and increasing-chord drawings of
  3-connected planar graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0315)
-/

open Set
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture

/-- The union of the closed straight-line segments representing the edges of `G` under `f`. -/
def edgeTrace {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) : Set ℝ² :=
  {p | ∃ u v, G.Adj u v ∧ p ∈ segment ℝ (f u) (f v)}

/-- A crossing-free straight-line drawing has distinct vertex positions, and two drawn edges meet
only at positions that are endpoints of both edges. -/
def IsPlanarDrawing {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧
    ∀ ⦃u v x y⦄, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y →
      ({u, v} : Set V) = {x, y} ∨
        segment ℝ (f u) (f v) ∩ segment ℝ (f x) (f y) ⊆
          ({f u, f v} : Set ℝ²) ∩ {f x, f y}

/-- A finite simple graph is planar if it has a crossing-free straight-line drawing in the plane. -/
def IsPlanar {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℝ², IsPlanarDrawing G f

/-- A graph is 3-vertex-connected if deleting any set of fewer than three vertices leaves a
connected graph. -/
def IsThreeConnected {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset V, S.card < 3 → (G.induce (↑S : Set V)ᶜ).Connected

/-- A polyhedral graph is a finite simple, planar, 3-vertex-connected graph with at least four
vertices. Simplicity is built into `SimpleGraph`. -/
def IsPolyhedral {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  4 ≤ Fintype.card V ∧ IsThreeConnected G ∧ IsPlanar G

/-- A drawing is greedy if, from any vertex other than the target, an adjacent vertex is strictly
closer to the target in Euclidean distance. -/
def IsGreedyDrawing {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x t⦄, x ≠ t → ∃ y, G.Adj x y ∧ dist (f y) (f t) < dist (f x) (f t)

/-- Every face of the straight-line drawing is bounded by a convex polygon. Faces are the connected
components of the complement of the edge trace. This condition applies also to the unbounded outer
face, whose boundary (rather than its unbounded region) is a convex polygon. -/
def HasConvexFaces {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∉ edgeTrace G f, ∃ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → V),
    3 ≤ n ∧ Function.Injective v ∧
      (∀ i, G.Adj (v i) (v (finRotate n i))) ∧
      frontier (connectedComponentIn (edgeTrace G f)ᶜ x) =
        ⋃ i, segment ℝ (f (v i)) (f (v (finRotate n i))) ∧
      frontier (convexHull ℝ (Set.range fun i ↦ f (v i))) =
        ⋃ i, segment ℝ (f (v i)) (f (v (finRotate n i)))

/-- A convex greedy embedding is a crossing-free straight-line greedy drawing all of whose faces,
including the outer face, are bounded by convex polygons. -/
def IsConvexGreedyEmbedding {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  IsPlanarDrawing G f ∧ IsGreedyDrawing G f ∧ HasConvexFaces G f

/--
The strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture: every finite simple 3-connected planar graph (that
is, every polyhedral graph) has a straight-line embedding in the Euclidean plane that is greedy,
has no edge crossings, and has convex boundaries for every face, including the outer face.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem strong_papadimitriou_ratajczak_conjecture :
    ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), IsPolyhedral G →
      ∃ f : V → ℝ², IsConvexGreedyEmbedding G f := by
  sorry

end StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “polyhedral graph” as a finite simple 3-vertex-connected planar graph with at least four vertices, following the background article and Steinitz equivalence stated in the decomposition.

Because Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no planar graph or straight-line graph-drawing primitive, represented planarity by an injective placement in Euclidean ℝ² whose distinct closed edge segments intersect only at shared endpoints. For finite simple graphs this is equivalent to abstract planarity by Fáry's theorem.

Formalized greediness exactly as the local routing condition from the article: for every distinct current vertex and target, some adjacent vertex has strictly smaller Euclidean distance to the target.

Modeled faces as connected components of the complement of the union of drawn edge segments. Required each component boundary, including the unbounded outer component's boundary, to be both a simple cyclic union of graph-edge segments and the frontier of the convex hull of its cycle vertices.

Used the non-strict geometric notion of a convex polygon via equality of its edge boundary with the frontier of its convex hull; this avoids strengthening “convex” to the repository helper's strictly convex oriented-polygon condition.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture

Papadimitriou and Ratajczak conjectured that every polyhedral graph (a $3$-connected planar
graph) has a greedy embedding in the Euclidean plane. This weak form was proved by Leighton and
Moitra and by Angelini, Frati and Grilli. The greedy embeddings produced by these proofs may have
crossing edges. The *strong* Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture asks for a planar greedy embedding
in which every face is convex. It is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Greedy embedding § Planar graphs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greedy_embedding%23Planar_graphs)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [PR05] Papadimitriou, C. H. and Ratajczak, D., *On a conjecture related to geometric routing*.
  Theoret. Comput. Sci. 344 (2005), 3–14.
- [LM10] Leighton, T. and Moitra, A., *Some results on greedy embeddings in metric spaces*.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. 44 (2010), 686–705.
- [NPR16] Nöllenburg, M., Prutkin, R. and Rutter, I., *On self-approaching and increasing-chord
  drawings of 3-connected planar graphs*. J. Comput. Geom. 7 (2016), 47–69.
  [arXiv:1409.0315](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0315)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry

namespace StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture

variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²)

/-- The point set of the straight-line drawing of `G` with vertex positions `f`: the vertex
points together with the closed segment joining the endpoints of every edge. -/
def drawing : Set ℝ² :=
  Set.range f ∪ ⋃ (a) (b) (_ : G.Adj a b), segment ℝ (f a) (f b)

/-- The vertex positions `f` give a *plane* straight-line drawing of `G` (a straight-line drawing
without edge crossings): vertices are placed at distinct points, no vertex lies on an edge that is
not incident to it, and two distinct edges meet only in their common endpoints. -/
structure IsPlaneDrawing : Prop where
  injective : Function.Injective f
  notMem_segment : ∀ a b w, G.Adj a b → w ≠ a → w ≠ b → f w ∉ segment ℝ (f a) (f b)
  segment_inter_subset : ∀ a b c d, G.Adj a b → G.Adj c d → s(a, b) ≠ s(c, d) →
    segment ℝ (f a) (f b) ∩ segment ℝ (f c) (f d) ⊆ {f a, f b} ∩ {f c, f d}

/-- The faces of the drawing of `G` with vertex positions `f`: the connected components of the
complement of the drawing in the plane. Exactly one face is unbounded; it is the outer face. -/
def faces : Set (Set ℝ²) :=
  {F | ∃ x ∉ drawing G f, F = connectedComponentIn (drawing G f)ᶜ x}

/-- Every face of the drawing of `G` with vertex positions `f` is convex. A bounded face is a
convex set. The outer face is bounded by a convex polygon, i.e. its complement is a convex set. -/
def HasConvexFaces : Prop :=
  ∀ F ∈ faces G f,
    (Bornology.IsBounded F → Convex ℝ F) ∧ (¬ Bornology.IsBounded F → Convex ℝ Fᶜ)

/-- The vertex positions `f` give a *greedy embedding* (greedy drawing) of `G` in the Euclidean
plane: for every two distinct vertices `x ≠ t`, some neighbour `y` of `x` is strictly closer to
`t` than `x` is. Hence greedy routing from `x` to `t` never gets stuck. -/
def IsGreedyDrawing : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, x ≠ t → ∃ y, G.Adj x y ∧ dist (f y) (f t) < dist (f x) (f t)

/-- The vertex positions `f` give a *convex greedy embedding* of `G`: a plane straight-line
drawing with convex faces that is a greedy embedding. -/
def IsConvexGreedyDrawing : Prop :=
  IsPlaneDrawing G f ∧ HasConvexFaces G f ∧ IsGreedyDrawing G f

/-- A finite simple graph is *polyhedral* if it is planar and $3$-vertex-connected. By Steinitz's
theorem these are exactly the graphs of vertices and edges of convex polyhedra. By Fáry's theorem
a finite simple graph is planar if and only if it has a plane straight-line drawing, which is how
planarity is expressed here. Note that `IsKConnected G 3` requires more than $3$ vertices. -/
def IsPolyhedral [Fintype V] : Prop :=
  G.IsKConnected 3 ∧ ∃ f : V → ℝ², IsPlaneDrawing G f

/-- A greedy drawing places distinct vertices at distinct points. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem IsGreedyDrawing.injective {G : SimpleGraph V} {f : V → ℝ²} (h : IsGreedyDrawing G f) :
    Function.Injective f := by
  intro x t hxt
  by_contra hne
  obtain ⟨y, -, hy⟩ := h x t hne
  rw [hxt, dist_self] at hy
  exact (dist_nonneg).not_gt hy

/-- A polyhedral graph has at least $4$ vertices. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem IsPolyhedral.four_le_card [Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} (h : IsPolyhedral G) :
    4 ≤ Fintype.card V :=
  h.1.1

/-- **The strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture.** Every polyhedral graph, i.e. every finite
$3$-connected planar graph, has a convex greedy embedding: a straight-line drawing in the
Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ without edge crossings, in which every face (including the outer
face) is a convex polygon, and such that for every two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ some neighbour
$y$ of $x$ satisfies $d(y, t) < d(x, t)$ for the Euclidean distance $d$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52 68]
theorem strong_papadimitriou_ratajczak_conjecture {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (hG : IsPolyhedral G) : ∃ f : V → ℝ², IsConvexGreedyDrawing G f := by
  sorry

end StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (3-connected planar finite simple graph; straight-line planar drawing with all faces including the outer face convex; strict greedy condition over x ≠ t) match the Wikipedia article and Nöllenburg–Prutkin–Rutter, and the file conforms to them.
modeling_decisions: Planarity of the input graph is expressed as the existence of a crossing-free straight-line drawing (∃ f, IsPlaneDrawing G f). By Fáry's theorem this is equivalent to topological planarity for finite simple graphs; Mathlib has no planarity notion.

3-connectivity uses the repo's SimpleGraph.IsKConnected G 3, which requires more than 3 vertices and connectivity after deleting any fewer than 3 vertices (standard convention; K₄ is the smallest polyhedral graph). Steinitz's characterization (graph of a convex polyhedron) is only mentioned in the docstring, not formalized.

Faces are the connected components of ℝ² minus the drawing (vertex points ∪ closed edge segments). 'Every face convex' is: every bounded face is a convex set, and the unbounded (outer) face has a convex complement (i.e. the outer boundary is a convex polygon). The outer face is included, following the standard meaning of a convex drawing and the decomposition notes.
Convexity is non-strict (Convex ℝ), so a face may have a 180° angle at a vertex; this matches 'convex polygon' / Tutte-style convex drawings rather than 'strictly convex'.

Greedy condition quantifies over distinct vertices x ≠ t (Wikipedia's 'for every two nodes x and t' is impossible for x = t) with a strict inequality in the Euclidean metric of ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2). Greedy implies injectivity (proved as an API lemma), and IsPlaneDrawing also requires injectivity, matching 'vertices mapped to distinct points'.

The crossing-freeness condition is stated on unordered edges s(a,b) ≠ s(c,d): segment ∩ segment ⊆ {f a, f b} ∩ {f c, f d}; with injectivity this forbids proper crossings, overlaps of collinear edges, and (with the separate notMem_segment field) vertices lying on non-incident edges.
The weak (proved) Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture is described only in the module docstring as background and not stated as a declaration, per the decomposition notes.

open Set SimpleGraph
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/-- A finite graph is three-vertex-connected if it has at least four vertices and remains
connected after deleting any set of fewer than three vertices. -/
def IsThreeConnected {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  4 ≤ Fintype.card V ∧ ∀ s : Set V, s.ncard < 3 → (G.induce sᶜ).Connected

/-- The subset of the plane covered by the straight edges of the drawing `p` of `G`. -/
def edgeImage {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²) : Set ℝ² :=
  {q | ∃ u v, G.Adj u v ∧ q ∈ segment ℝ (p u) (p v)}

/-- An injective straight-line drawing is planar if distinct edge segments meet only at the
positions of their common endpoints. -/
def IsPlanarDrawing {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective p ∧
    ∀ ⦃u v w z : V⦄, G.Adj u v → G.Adj w z → ({u, v} : Set V) ≠ {w, z} →
      segment ℝ (p u) (p v) ∩ segment ℝ (p w) (p z) ⊆
        p '' (({u, v} : Set V) ∩ {w, z})

/-- A finite graph is planar if it has an injective crossing-free straight-line drawing in the
Euclidean plane. -/
def IsPlanar {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : V → ℝ², IsPlanarDrawing G p

/-- Every face of a straight-line drawing, including the outer face, is a convex polygon.
Faces are the connected components of the complement of the drawn edges. Their polygonal
boundaries are characterized as boundaries of the convex hulls of their incident vertices. -/
def HasConvexFaces {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ (edgeImage G p)ᶜ,
    let face := connectedComponentIn (edgeImage G p)ᶜ x
    frontier face = frontier (convexHull ℝ (p '' {v | p v ∈ frontier face}))

/-- A drawing is greedy if, for every current vertex `x` and distinct target vertex `t`, some
neighbor of `x` is strictly closer in Euclidean distance to `t`. -/
def IsGreedyDrawing {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x t : V⦄, x ≠ t → ∃ y, G.Adj x y ∧ dist (p y) (p t) < dist (p x) (p t)

/--
The strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture: every finite simple three-connected planar graph
has an injective straight-line embedding in the Euclidean plane which is planar, is greedy, and
has every face, including the outer face, bounded by a convex polygon.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem strong_papadimitriou_ratajczak_conjecture :
    ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), IsThreeConnected G → IsPlanar G →
      ∃ p : V → ℝ², IsPlanarDrawing G p ∧ HasConvexFaces G p ∧ IsGreedyDrawing G p := by
  sorry

end StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture
modeling_decisions: Following the background article, “polyhedral graph” is modeled as a finite simple planar graph that is 3-vertex-connected and has at least four vertices.
Three-vertex-connectivity is stated by requiring that deletion of every vertex set of cardinality less than three leaves a connected induced graph.

Abstract planarity is modeled by existence of an injective straight-line Euclidean-plane drawing in which distinct edge segments intersect only at positions of common endpoints; for finite simple graphs this is equivalent to ordinary graph planarity by Fáry's theorem.
A face is modeled as a connected component of the complement of the union of all drawn closed edge segments.

A face boundary is convex when it equals the frontier of the convex hull of the drawn vertices lying on that boundary. This formulation handles bounded faces and the outer face uniformly: it requires the outer face's boundary polygon to be convex without incorrectly requiring its unbounded region to be convex.
The greedy condition uses strict Euclidean distance decrease and is required for every ordered pair of distinct vertices, exactly as in the article.

abbrev Plane := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

/-- The set in the Euclidean plane covered by the straight edges of a drawing `p` of `G`. -/
def drawnEdges {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → Plane) : Set Plane :=
  {z | ∃ u v, G.Adj u v ∧ z ∈ segment ℝ (p u) (p v)}

/-- A straight-line drawing is plane if vertices have distinct positions and two distinct edges
intersect only at the position of a common endpoint. -/
def IsPlaneDrawing {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (p : V → Plane) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective p ∧
    ∀ ⦃u v x y : V⦄, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y → s(u, v) ≠ s(x, y) →
      ∀ z ∈ segment ℝ (p u) (p v) ∩ segment ℝ (p x) (p y),
        ∃ w, (w = u ∨ w = v) ∧ (w = x ∨ w = y) ∧ z = p w

face, is the boundary of its convex hull. Faces are the connected components of the complement

A *greedy embedding* of a graph in the Euclidean plane assigns a point of the plane to every
vertex so that for every two distinct vertices $x$ and $t$ some neighbour $y$ of $x$ is strictly
closer to $t$ than $x$ is. Papadimitriou and Ratajczak conjectured that every polyhedral graph

proved by Leighton and Moitra and by Angelini, Frati and Grilli.

*convex greedy embedding*, that is, a greedy embedding that is also a planar straight-line drawing
in which every face, including the outer face, is a convex polygon. This is open.

    ∀ ⦃u v x y⦄, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y →
      segment ℝ (p u) (p v) ∩ segment ℝ (p x) (p y) ⊆
        p '' ({u, v} ∩ {x, y})

  ∃ p : V → ℝ², IsPlanarDrawing G p

complement of its edge carrier. For a bounded face its closure is required to be convex. For the
unbounded outer face, the complement of its closure (the interior of its boundary polygon) is
required to be convex. -/

  ∀ q ∉ drawingCarrier G p,

      Convex ℝ (closure (connectedComponentIn (drawingCarrier G p)ᶜ q))ᶜ

is strictly closer in Euclidean distance to the target. -/

  ∀ ⦃x t⦄, x ≠ t → ∃ y, G.Adj x y ∧ dist (p y) (p t) < dist (p x) (p t)

/-!
# Strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Greedy embedding § Planar graphs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greedy_embedding%23Planar_graphs)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [PR05] Papadimitriou, C. H. and Ratajczak, D., *On a conjecture related to geometric routing*,
  Theoret. Comput. Sci. 344 (2005), 3–14.
- [NP13] Nöllenburg, M. and Prutkin, R., *Euclidean greedy drawings of trees*, Proc. 21st European
  Symposium on Algorithms (ESA 2013). [arXiv:1306.5224](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.5224)
- [NPR16] Nöllenburg, M., Prutkin, R. and Rutter, I., *On self-approaching and increasing-chord
  drawings of 3-connected planar graphs*, J. Comput. Geom. 7 (2016), 47–69.
  [arXiv:1409.0315](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0315)

A *greedy embedding* of a graph in the Euclidean plane assigns a point to every vertex so that
for every two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ some neighbour $y$ of $x$ is strictly closer to $t$
than $x$ is. Papadimitriou and Ratajczak [PR05] conjectured that every polyhedral graph
(3-connected planar graph, equivalently the graph of a convex polyhedron) has a greedy embedding
in the Euclidean plane; this was proved by Leighton–Moitra and by Angelini–Frati–Grilli.
The greedy embeddings produced by these proofs need not be planar drawings.

The *strong* Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture, which remains open, asserts that every
polyhedral graph has a *convex greedy embedding*: a planar straight-line drawing that is greedy
and in which every face, including the outer face, is a convex polygon [PR05, NP13, NPR16].

## Formalisation choices

- Drawings are straight-line: a drawing is a map from the vertices to $\mathbb{R}^2$, and every
  edge is drawn as the closed segment between the images of its endpoints. This is the setting
  of greedy embeddings, where only the vertex positions matter.
- Mathlib has no notion of planar graph. Since every graph considered here is finite and simple,
  we use Fáry's theorem and call a graph planar if it admits a planar straight-line drawing,
  that is, a drawing with distinct vertex positions in which no vertex lies on a non-incident
  edge and two distinct edges meet only in common endpoints.
- The faces of a planar straight-line drawing are the connected components of the complement of
  the drawing in the plane. A face is a convex polygon if it is a convex set (bounded faces), or,
  for the unbounded outer face, if its complement (the closed region enclosed by the outer
  boundary) is a convex set.
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry
open SimpleGraph

namespace StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture

variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²)

/-- The set of points of the plane covered by the straight-line drawing of `G` with vertex
positions `p`: the vertex points together with the closed segment joining the endpoints of every
edge. -/
def drawing : Set ℝ² :=
  Set.range p ∪ ⋃ (u : V) (v : V) (_ : G.Adj u v), segment ℝ (p u) (p v)

/-- `p` is a planar straight-line drawing of `G`: distinct vertices are drawn at distinct points,
no vertex lies on the segment drawing an edge unless it is an endpoint of that edge, and the
segments drawing two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints. -/
def IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing : Prop :=
  Function.Injective p ∧
  (∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → p w ∈ segment ℝ (p u) (p v) → w = u ∨ w = v) ∧
  (∀ u v x y, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y → s(u, v) ≠ s(x, y) →
    segment ℝ (p u) (p v) ∩ segment ℝ (p x) (p y) ⊆ p '' ({u, v} ∩ {x, y}))

/-- A finite simple graph is *polyhedral* if it is 3-connected and planar. By Steinitz's theorem
these are exactly the graphs of vertices and edges of convex polyhedra. Planarity is expressed,
via Fáry's theorem, as the existence of a planar straight-line drawing. -/
def IsPolyhedral [Fintype V] : Prop :=
  G.IsKConnected 3 ∧ ∃ p : V → ℝ², IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G p

/-- The vertex positions `p` form a *greedy embedding* of `G` in the Euclidean plane: for every
two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ there is a neighbour $y$ of $x$ with $d(y, t) < d(x, t)$. -/
def IsGreedy : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, x ≠ t → ∃ y, G.Adj x y ∧ dist (p y) (p t) < dist (p x) (p t)

/-- Every face of the drawing of `G` with vertex positions `p` is a convex polygon. The faces are
the connected components of the complement of the drawing. A bounded face is required to be a
convex set; the unbounded (outer) face is required to have convex complement, i.e. the closed
region enclosed by the outer boundary is convex. -/
def HasConvexFaces : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∉ drawing G p,
    (Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x) →
      Convex ℝ (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x)) ∧
    (¬ Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x) →
      Convex ℝ (connectedComponentIn (drawing G p)ᶜ x)ᶜ)

/-- `p` is a *convex greedy embedding* of `G`: a planar straight-line drawing of `G` in which
every face (including the outer face) is a convex polygon and which is greedy. -/
def IsConvexGreedyEmbedding : Prop :=
  IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G p ∧ HasConvexFaces G p ∧ IsGreedy G p

/-- A greedy embedding of the complete graph is given by any injective vertex placement. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem isGreedy_top (hp : Function.Injective p) : IsGreedy (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) p := by
  intro x t hxt
  exact ⟨t, hxt, by simpa using dist_pos.mpr (hp.ne hxt)⟩

/-- The empty graph on at least two vertices has no greedy embedding. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem not_isGreedy_bot [Nontrivial V] : ¬ IsGreedy (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) p := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨x, t, hxt⟩ := exists_pair_ne V
  obtain ⟨y, hy, -⟩ := h x t hxt
  exact hy

/-- Any injective vertex placement is a planar straight-line drawing of the empty graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem isPlanarStraightLineDrawing_bot (hp : Function.Injective p) :
    IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) p :=
  ⟨hp, fun _ _ _ h => h.elim, fun _ _ _ _ h => h.elim⟩

/-- A graph on at most three vertices is not polyhedral. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem not_isPolyhedral_of_card_le [Fintype V] (h : Fintype.card V ≤ 3) : ¬ IsPolyhedral G :=
  fun hG => not_isKConnected_of_card_le h hG.1

/-- **Strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture** [PR05]. Every polyhedral graph, i.e. every
finite simple 3-connected planar graph, has a convex greedy embedding in the Euclidean plane:
a planar straight-line drawing in which every face (including the outer face) is a convex
polygon and such that for every two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ some neighbour $y$ of $x$
satisfies $d(y, t) < d(x, t)$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem strong_papadimitriou_ratajczak_conjecture [Fintype V] (hG : IsPolyhedral G) :
    ∃ p : V → ℝ², IsConvexGreedyEmbedding G p := by
  sorry

end StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture

vertices such that for every two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ some neighbour $y$ of $x$ is strictly
closer to $t$ than $x$ is. Papadimitriou and Ratajczak conjectured that every polyhedral graph
(finite, simple, $3$-connected, planar) has a greedy embedding in the Euclidean plane; this was
proved by Leighton and Moitra and, independently, by Angelini, Frati and Grilli. The *strong*
form of the conjecture, which remains open, asks moreover for a *convex* greedy embedding: a
planar straight-line drawing (no two edges cross) in which every face, including the outer face,
is a convex polygon.

Following [NPR16], all drawings are straight-line drawings with vertices at distinct points.
The faces of such a drawing are the connected components of the complement of the drawing in the
plane. For a bounded face, convexity means that the face is a convex set; for the unbounded (outer)
face it means that the region enclosed by the drawing, i.e. the complement of the outer face, is a
convex set.

drawing; by Fáry's theorem this is equivalent to the usual topological notion.

open Bornology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace StrongPapadimitriouRatajczakConjecture

variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²)

/-- The straight-line drawing of `G` with vertex positions `f`, viewed as a subset of the plane:
the positions of the vertices together with the closed segments joining the positions of
adjacent vertices. -/
def drawing : Set ℝ² :=
  Set.range f ∪ ⋃ (u : V) (v : V) (_ : G.Adj u v), segment ℝ (f u) (f v)

/-- `f` is a *planar straight-line drawing* of `G`: vertices are mapped to distinct points,
no vertex lies on the segment of an edge not incident to it, and two distinct edges meet only
at the position of a common endpoint (in particular, non-incident edges do not cross). -/
structure IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing : Prop where
  injective : Function.Injective f
  notMem_segment : ∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → w ≠ u → w ≠ v → f w ∉ segment ℝ (f u) (f v)
  inter_segment : ∀ a b c d, G.Adj a b → G.Adj c d → s(a, b) ≠ s(c, d) →
    ∀ p ∈ segment ℝ (f a) (f b) ∩ segment ℝ (f c) (f d), ∃ w, w ∈ s(a, b) ∧ w ∈ s(c, d) ∧ f w = p

/-- A simple graph is *planar* if it admits a planar straight-line drawing in the Euclidean
plane. For finite graphs, this agrees with the topological notion by Fáry's theorem. -/
def Planar : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℝ², IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G f

variable [Fintype V] in
/-- A finite simple graph is *polyhedral* if it is $3$-connected and planar. By Steinitz's
theorem these are exactly the graphs of vertices and edges of convex polyhedra. Note that
`G.IsKConnected 3` requires `G` to have more than three vertices. -/
def IsPolyhedral : Prop :=
  G.IsKConnected 3 ∧ Planar G

variable {G} in
/-- A polyhedral graph has more than three vertices; `K_4` is the smallest one. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsPolyhedral.three_lt_card [Fintype V] (hG : IsPolyhedral G) : 3 < Fintype.card V :=
  hG.1.1

/-- The vertex positions `f` form a *greedy drawing* (greedy embedding) of `G` in the Euclidean
plane: for every two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ there is a neighbour $y$ of $x$ with
$d(y, t) < d(x, t)$, where $d$ is the Euclidean distance. -/
def IsGreedyDrawing : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, x ≠ t → ∃ y, G.Adj x y ∧ dist (f y) (f t) < dist (f x) (f t)

variable {G f} in
/-- The vertex positions of a greedy drawing are pairwise distinct. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsGreedyDrawing.injective (h : IsGreedyDrawing G f) : Function.Injective f := by
  intro x t hxt
  by_contra hne
  obtain ⟨y, -, hy⟩ := h x t hne
  rw [hxt, dist_self] at hy
  exact absurd hy (not_lt.mpr dist_nonneg)

/-- `F` is a *face* of the straight-line drawing of `G` with vertex positions `f`: a connected
component of the complement of the drawing in the plane. -/
def IsFace (F : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ p ∉ drawing G f, F = connectedComponentIn (drawing G f)ᶜ p

/-- Every face of the straight-line drawing of `G` with vertex positions `f` is convex: every
bounded face is a convex set, and the region enclosed by the drawing, i.e. the complement of the
unbounded (outer) face, is a convex set. -/
def HasConvexFaces : Prop :=
  ∀ F, IsFace G f F → (IsBounded F → Convex ℝ F) ∧ (¬ IsBounded F → Convex ℝ Fᶜ)

/--
**The strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture.** Every polyhedral graph (every finite simple
$3$-connected planar graph) has a convex greedy embedding in the Euclidean plane: there is a
planar straight-line drawing of the graph, with vertices at distinct points, that is greedy
(for every two distinct vertices $x \neq t$ some neighbour $y$ of $x$ satisfies
$d(y, t) < d(x, t)$) and in which every face, including the outer face, is a convex polygon.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem strong_papadimitriou_ratajczak_conjecture [Fintype V] (hG : IsPolyhedral G) :
    ∃ f : V → ℝ², IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G f ∧ IsGreedyDrawing G f ∧ HasConvexFaces G f := by

modeling_decisions: Planarity of G is defined as the existence of a crossing-free straight-line drawing (Fáry's theorem makes this equivalent to topological planarity for finite simple graphs). Mathlib has no planar-graph notion; this avoids topological embeddings or Kuratowski minors.

Drawings are straight-line with vertices at distinct points, following Nöllenburg–Prutkin(–Rutter) ('all drawings are straight-line and vertices are mapped to distinct points'); the greedy condition itself forces distinct positions (API lemma IsGreedyDrawing.injective).

Greedy is formalized as the 'closer neighbour' condition ∀ x ≠ t, ∃ y ~ x, d(y,t) < d(x,t) (Wikipedia's definition); for finite graphs with distinct positions this is equivalent to the 'distance-decreasing path' formulation of NPR16.

Faces are the connected components of ℝ² minus the drawing (vertex points ∪ edge segments). Convexity: bounded faces must be convex sets; for the unbounded (outer) face the complement must be convex, which is the standard meaning of 'the outer face is a convex polygon'. Non-strict convexity is used (angles of π allowed), as in 'convex drawing'; 'strictly convex' is a stronger notion not asked for.
Including Set.range f in the drawing is irrelevant for polyhedral graphs (every vertex lies on an edge) but keeps the face definition correct for general graphs.

The field notMem_segment (no vertex on a non-incident edge) is implied by injectivity + inter_segment whenever every vertex has an incident edge (true for 3-connected graphs); it is kept so IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing is the standard notion for arbitrary graphs.

The planar-drawing requirement in the conclusion is kept even though planarity is also a hypothesis: the hypothesis says G is planar; the conclusion says the specific greedy drawing is planar, which is the content of the 'strong' conjecture.
SimpleGraph.IsKConnected G 3 requires 3 < card V, so IsPolyhedral excludes graphs with ≤ 3 vertices, consistent with K4 being the smallest polyhedral graph (API lemma IsPolyhedral.three_lt_card).
Definitions were placed in the problem file (the sandbox permits only one file); Planar / IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing are reusable and could be moved to FormalConjecturesForMathlib by a reviewer.
